name: cellular phone
source: 'Exists' means a commercial product and service, not a prototype: Motorola's first handheld call was made on 3 April 1973, but the first US commercial cellular service opened in Chicago on 13 October 1983 and in the Washington-Baltimore area that December, with the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X approved in 1983 (Motorola and Smithsonian notes in the codex, Appendix D). Saint Jude is assumed to follow in early 1984; 'common' is a loose estimate.

name: car phone
source: Bell System Mobile Telephone Service began in St. Louis in June 1946; the improved IMTS followed in 1964. Always expensive and limited to a few channels per city.

name: pager
source: Al Gross's hospital pager dates from 1949; Motorola's Pageboy I tone-only pager was released in 1964. By 1980 pagers are used in some professional and business circles; they are never routine for ordinary people in the period.

name: numeric display pager
source: Bible section A6 puts numeric pagers as a street tool in the early to mid 1980s; the exact first date is approximate.

name: fax machine
source: Xerox's Long Distance Xerography (1964) and the Magnafax Telecopier (1966) were slow office machines; Group 3 machines in 1980 and falling prices brought wide adoption in the mid 1980s (codex Appendix A: wider adoption 1986-89).

name: videocassette recorder
source: Sony's U-matic arrived in 1971; Betamax reached the US in November 1975 and VHS in 1977. Ownership became visible in the early 1980s and common in the mid 1980s (codex Appendix A: video ownership and rental more visible 1984-85).

name: video rental store
source: The first prerecorded-tape sales and rental shops opened in 1977-78 in Michigan and Los Angeles; the bible section A6 gates VHS duplication to 1977 onward and small in 1980.

name: answering machine
source: Early machines were sold from the late 1940s; the consumer Phone-Mate machine arrived in 1971. Human answering services remain routine throughout (codex Appendix A3).

name: answering service
source: A human switchboard service, routine by 1980 (codex Appendix A3). The dates are loose estimates.

name: portable tape recorder
source: Philips introduced the compact cassette in August 1963; portable recorders were affordable by the late 1960s. Reel-to-reel recorders were used earlier (codex Appendix A).

name: body recorder
source: Nagra recorders date from 1951 (the codex names the Nagra body recorder); federal agencies and prosecutors use them on informants from the 1960s. Availability to ordinary people is not claimed.

name: closed-circuit camera
source: Closed-circuit television exists at specific sites in 1980 (codex A3 and A4); a modern, citywide camera network does not, and is not modelled before 1990.

name: personal computer
source: The Altair 8800 was announced in January 1975; the Apple II went on sale in June 1977 and the IBM PC in August 1981. Specialist workplaces first; wider adoption from 1986 (codex Appendix A).

name: office photocopier
source: The Xerox 914 was shown in September 1959 (codex Appendix A lists office photocopiers by 1980). 'Common' is an estimate.

name: automatic teller machine
source: The first cash machine ran at a Barclays branch in London in June 1967; Chemical Bank installed the first US machines in New York in September 1969. Spread through the 1970s; 'common' is an estimate.

name: bank credit card
source: BankAmericard launched in September 1958 and the Interbank (Master Charge) association in 1966. 'Common' is an estimate; no credit-card authorisation threshold is universal (codex A5).

name: arcade video game
source: Computer Space (1971) and Pong (November 1972) began the coin-operated video game; Space Invaders (1978) made arcades a routine amusement-route business. The bible section A6 gates it to the late 1970s.

name: Pac-Man
source: Released in Japan in May 1980 and in North America in October 1980 (bible section A6).

name: Atlantic City casino
source: Resorts International opened as the first legal casino in Atlantic City on 26 May 1978 (bible section A6 gates Atlantic City junkets to 1978 onward).

name: compact disc
source: Compact disc players went on sale in Japan in October 1982 and in the US in March 1983; wide adoption by about 1990.

name: Lincoln Town Car
source: The Town Car name replaced the Continental Town Car for the 1981 model year, on sale from late 1980 (codex A5 says it is not a default 1980 vehicle). Estimate.

name: Title III wiretap
source: Title III of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act, signed 19 June 1968, set up court-authorised wiretaps and bugs for federal and state officials; use stays constrained by law, evidence, staffing and budgets (codex A4). Routine use against organised crime grew through the 1970s and 1980s.

name: pen register
source: United States v. New York Telephone Co. (7 December 1977) upheld court orders for pen registers; Smith v. Maryland (1979) held that no warrant was needed. Telephone company records of calls placed exist well before this. Estimate for the early date.

name: RICO
aliases: Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act
source: Title IX of the Organized Crime Control Act of 1970, signed 15 October 1970 (codex A4: RICO exists in the early 1980s). Early prosecutions were few and cautious; systematic use against Mafia families grew in the early 1980s, so 'available' and 'common' are estimates.

name: RICO prosecution of a crime family
source: Federal prosecutors first used RICO against Mafia leadership in the late 1970s and made it routine in the early 1980s; the Commission case followed in 1985. These dates are rough estimates for a fictional city.

name: Witness Security Program
source: Authorised by the Organized Crime Control Act of 1970 (signed 15 October 1970); the US Marshals Service has run it since 1971. Never routine; it is a tool of federal prosecutors.

name: Bank Secrecy Act
source: Currency and Foreign Transactions Reporting Act, signed 26 October 1970, requires banks to report large cash transactions; enforcement was patchy until the 1980s. 'Common' is an estimate.

name: money laundering statute
source: The Money Laundering Control Act of 1986, signed 27 October 1986, made laundering itself a federal crime. Before it, prosecutors used the Bank Secrecy Act, tax and conspiracy charges. Washing cash through a front is an offence in a hazier sense before then.

name: federal preventive detention
source: The Comprehensive Crime Control Act of 1984, including the Bail Reform Act, was signed 12 October 1984 (codex A4 and A5: do not apply it to a case that predates it).

name: forensic DNA profiling
source: Alec Jeffreys announced DNA fingerprinting in 1984; the first US criminal conviction using DNA evidence came in Florida in November 1987 (codex A4: not a routine tool in 1980). 'Common' is an estimate.

name: crack cocaine
source: Retail crack markets are a mid-1980s development (bible section A6). Approximate dates.

name: TEC-9
source: Intratec's TEC-9 pistol was introduced in 1985 (the codex's use of it for earlier years was an anachronism; see the adaptation notes). Estimate for the 'common' date.
